requirements.quote:
+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+
    /                     CNAME                     /
    /                                               /
    +--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+

where:

CNAME           A <domain-name> which specifies the canonical or primary
                name for the owner.  The owner name is an alias.
requirements.condition: Encoding or decoding the RDATA of a CNAME resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the RDATA as one CNAME field containing a domain name.
requirements.why_checkable: The CNAME RDATA encoder and decoder can be checked for the single domain-name field shown in the format.

requirements.quote:
CNAME           A <domain-name> which specifies the canonical or primary
                name for the owner.  The owner name is an alias.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the record owner as an alias for the canonical or primary name specified by the CNAME domain-name value.
requirements.why_checkable: The alias mapping can be checked to ensure that it points from the owner to the canonical name carried in RDATA.

requirements.quote: CNAME RRs cause no additional section processing
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Trigger additional-section processing because of the CNAME resource record.
requirements.why_checkable: Additional-section generation can be inspected or exercised to verify that a CNAME record does not itself trigger that processing.

requirements.quote:
CNAME RRs cause no additional section processing, but name servers may
choose to restart the query at the canonical name in certain cases.  See
the description of name server logic in [RFC-1034] for details.
requirements.condition: A name server encounters a CNAME record in one of the certain cases referenced but not specified in this chunk.
requirements.required_behavior: The name server may choose to restart the query at the canonical name; the restart is permitted rather than required.
requirements.why_checkable: A query restart and its target would be observable, but the applicable cases are delegated to RFC-1034 and cannot be established from this chunk alone.
